comments.author: Sy0307
comments.body:
## Recipe quick start

Full recipe: [`recipes/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2_5.md`](https://github.com/Sy0307/vllm-omni/blob/feat/indextts-2.5-support/recipes/IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2_5.md)

### 1. Install

```bash
pip install -e '.[indextts2]'
```

Prepare the native IndexTTS 2.5 model bundle and a short, clean reference WAV for voice cloning.

### 2. Start the server

```bash
MODEL=/path/to/indextts-2.5

vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --omni \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8092 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --deploy-config vllm_omni/deploy/indextts2_5.yaml
```

### 3. Generate speech with a cloned voice

```bash
python examples/online_serving/text_to_speech/indextts2/speech_client.py \
  --api-base http://127.0.0.1:8092 \
  --model-version 2.5 \
  --model "$MODEL" \
  --ref-audio /path/to/reference.wav \
  --lang zh \
  --speed 1.0 \
  --text '你好，这是 IndexTTS 二点五语音合成测试。' \
  --output indextts2_5.wav
```

The same command supports:

- Native speed control: `--speed 0.5` through `--speed 2.0`.
- Languages: `--lang zh`, `en`, `zhen`, `ja`, or `yue`.
- Emotion vector: `--emo-vector 1 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 --emo-alpha 0.8`.
- Emotion text: `--use-emo-text --emo-text '开心、兴奋而且充满活力'`.
- Emotion reference audio: `--emo-audio /path/to/emotion.wav`.
- Pre-normalized text: add `--no-text-normalization`.

### 4. Optional named-voice reuse

Upload the reference audio once:

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8092/v1/audio/voices \
  -F 'audio_sample=@/path/to/reference.wav' \
  -F 'consent=user-consent-id' \
  -F 'name=indextts_demo_voice'
```

Then replace `--ref-audio ...` with:

```bash
--voice indextts_demo_voice
```

The validated output is 22.05 kHz mono WAV. H200 E2E covered voice cloning at 1.0x and 2.0x; Whisper-small matched the normalized input exactly for both files.

comments.author: linyueqian
comments.body:
On the benchmarking side: does IndexTTS 2.5 need the dedicated `benchmarks/tts/benchmark_indextts2_5.py`, or could it be a `model_configs.yaml` entry instead?

The registry header states the intent directly:

```
# Universal TTS benchmark model registry.
# To add a new TTS model: add an entry here. No code changes required.
```

Every other TTS model in that directory (Qwen3-TTS, Higgs v3, VoxCPM2, the MOSS-TTS family) is registered that way, so this would be the first per-model driver script.

The README gives two reasons for the dedicated driver, and both look already covered by the shared harness:

1. The bundled emotion-model tokenizer: `bench_tts.py:155` ends with `cmd += extra_cli_args`, fed by the `argparse.REMAINDER` at line 256, so `--tokenizer <path>` passes straight through to `vllm bench serve`.
2. IndexTTS specific `extra_params`: that is what `task_extra_body` is for, and Qwen3-TTS and MOSS already use it for their model specific request fields.

The shared path is also strictly more capable: `--wer-eval` for WER/SIM/UTMOS (line 242), `audio_underrun` in the default percentile metrics (line 124), and results that feed `plot_results.py`. A registry entry would look roughly like:

```yaml
  IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5:
    supported_tasks: [voice_clone]
    backend: openai-audio-speech
    endpoint: /v1/audio/speech
    trust_remote_code: true
    task_extra_body:
      voice_clone:
        extra_params:
          lang: en
          text_normalization: true
```

One genuine gap I hit while checking this: `bench_tts.py` hardcodes `--num-warmups 2` (lines 121 and 122) while your script exposes it as a flag. That seems better solved as an option on the shared harness so every model benefits, rather than as a reason to fork the driver.

One thing worth verifying rather than assuming: `bench_tts.py` resolves the model by its registry key, so serving from a local bundle path may need `--served-model-name` or a small key/path split. If that turns out to be awkward it is still likely a smaller change than maintaining a parallel driver plus its wrapper test.

The fixed n=500, concurrency 4/8/16/32 acceptance workload is worth keeping either way, just as a documented command in the README where the other models' reference workloads already live.

comments.author: hsliuustc0106
comments.body:
Blocking on two items:

1. The new-model validation evidence is incomplete. The H200 smoke/Whisper result is useful, but this PR does not include a profiler trace/peak-VRAM analysis or a same-hardware baseline against an authoritative IndexTTS 2.5 runner. The recipe links the HF model and mentions `num_beams=1`, but does not identify a native runner/source revision or provide baseline results. Please add profiler top ops, peak VRAM and a repeated-inference leak check, plus native-vs-vLLM latency/RTF, VRAM, and output-quality results on identical inputs. If no authoritative 2.5 runner is public, document that and provide the profiling evidence at minimum.

2. Native speed is rejected for streaming. `IndexTTS25Adapter` declares `native_speed_control` and maps `speed` to `duration_factor`, but [`_validate_speech_streaming_request()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/f515ee3f88d8030e2700a6364a97d5c278976cd2/vllm_omni/entrypoints/openai/serving_speech.py#L3691-L3695) rejects every `speed != 1.0` before raw or SSE streaming reaches adapter preparation. Exempt native-speed adapters from this generic restriction and add raw+SSE coverage.

Validation: all changed CPU/core tests passed locally (`459 passed, 22 warnings in 27.76s`) with Python 3.12.13, Torch 2.11.0+cu130, and vLLM 0.26.0. Real-checkpoint E2E/profiling was not reproducible because the IndexTTS 2.5 bundle is unavailable in the review environment.

comments.author: Sy0307
comments.body:
Thanks @linyueqian and @hsliuustc0106. I addressed the actionable code-review items in `11e49e89` (rebased onto the latest `main`):

### Shared TTS benchmark harness
- Removed the dedicated `benchmark_indextts2_5.py` driver and its dedicated test.
- Registered `IndexTeam/IndexTTS-2.5` in `benchmarks/tts/model_configs.yaml`.
- Kept the fixed acceptance sweep in the shared `bench_tts.py` workflow.
- Added generic `--num-warmups`, `--served-model-name`, and `--request-seed` options. The served-model override lets a registry key select defaults while the running server uses a local native bundle path.

### Native speed with raw/SSE responses
- Moved the streaming speed decision out of the global request schema and into the serving layer, where it can consult the model adapter capability.
- Models without native speed control still reject streaming `speed != 1.0`.
- Native-speed adapters accept it, and IndexTTS maps it to `duration_factor`.
- Added endpoint coverage for both raw audio and SSE paths.

Focused validation on the H200 environment after the rebase: **236 passed** across the shared benchmark CLI, speech serving, and TTS adapter test suites. Ruff format/check also pass locally.

I am still collecting the requested H200 profiler top-ops, peak-VRAM, and repeated-inference memory evidence. I will post those separately rather than treating the existing functional E2E result as sufficient performance validation. The official IndexTTS 2.5 native runner/checkpoint is not currently publicly reproducible, so any native-vs-vLLM comparison will be clearly scoped to an available pinned local bundle/source revision instead of presented as an authoritative upstream baseline.

comments.author: Sy0307
comments.body:
## Additional validation evidence

I collected the requested profiler and repeated-inference evidence on the current PR path. One correction to the earlier smoke-test wording: the remote host alias is `H200`, but `nvidia-smi` reports the physical device as **NVIDIA L20X, 143771 MiB**. I am therefore not presenting these results as H200 measurements.

### Functional quality

Fixed-seed Chinese request:

`今天天气很好，我们一起去公园散步，感受温暖的阳光。`

| Native speed | Output duration | Whisper-small transcript |
|---|---:|---|
| 1.0x | 5.503 s | 今天天气很好我们一起去公园散步感受温暖的阳光 |
| 2.0x | 2.752 s | 今天天气很好我们一起去公园散步感受温暖的阳光 |

Both outputs were 22,050 Hz mono WAV and matched the requested sentence after punctuation normalization.

### Peak VRAM and repeated-inference leak check

The standard two-stage deploy config was used on one L20X GPU. NVML was sampled every 50 ms during a profiled request:

- peak process/device memory: **59,845 MiB**
- peak sampled GPU utilization during the profiled request: **34%**
- profiler-instrumented request latency: 19.224 s (profiler overhead; not a serving number)

The stage-0 startup accounting reported 3.57 GiB weights, 0.13 GiB peak activation, 0.22 GiB non-Torch memory, 0.06 GiB CUDA graph memory, and a 52.0 GiB configured KV-cache allocation. The reported 59,845 MiB is therefore the configured serving footprint, not a claim that the weights require 60 GiB.

After one warmup, 10 sequential unprofiled requests produced:

`825, 772, 756, 732, 765, 771, 749, 750, 649, 767 ms`

Median: **760.5 ms**; min/max: **649/825 ms**. NVML reported **59,845 MiB after every request**, with no monotonic growth across the run.

### PyTorch profiler top CUDA operators

Stage 0 (AR talker), excluding the inclusive execution-context annotations:

| Operator/kernel | Self CUDA |
|---|---:|
| NVJet GEMM `64x8_64x16...bias_TNT` | 38.973 ms |
| NVJet split-K GEMM | 19.460 ms |
| NVJet GEMM `16x64_64x16...bias_TNN` | 16.989 ms |
| `kernel_unified_attention` | 12.185 ms |
| compiled FX graph | 12.402 ms |
| fused add + layer norm kernels | 8.556 / 7.680 ms |

Stage 1 (S2Mel + vocoder), excluding the inclusive execution-context annotations:

| Operator/kernel | Self CUDA / CUDA total |
|---|---:|
| `aten::cudnn_convolution` | 20.283 / 22.855 ms |
| `aten::cudnn_convolution_transpose` | 11.425 / 12.377 ms |
| `aten::mm` | 10.686 / 11.145 ms |
| NCHW-to-NHWC kernels | 8.129 ms |
| `flash_attn::_flash_attn_forward` | 7.185 / 7.648 ms |
| `aten::addmm` | 6.249 / 6.901 ms |

The complete local artifacts include per-stage gzipped Kineto traces, profiler tables, memory snapshots, the 50 ms NVML sample log, and the repeat-run TSV.

### Native-runner comparison boundary

I also rechecked the official public channels. The official `index-tts/index-tts` repository currently publishes download/runtime instructions for IndexTTS, IndexTTS-1.5, and IndexTTS-2, but not an authoritative IndexTTS-2.5 runner/source revision. The 2.5 HF endpoint is not publicly readable without authorization. We have a local 2.5 bundle and an unversioned reference-code snapshot, but using that as an “authoritative upstream baseline” would overstate its provenance.

For that reason I am providing the reproducible vLLM profiling, memory-stability, latency, and ASR evidence above, while explicitly not fabricating a native-vs-vLLM comparison until IndexTeam publishes or identifies a pinned public 2.5 runner.

reviews.author: linyueqian
reviews.body:
Re-ran the native speed path independently on a single Hopper class GPU (cc 9.0, 132 SM, 141 GB HBM3e per the CUDA runtime) at `11e49e899`, which differs from the current head only by a pre-commit budget line and the docs rebase.

Both items from the last round check out:

**Shared benchmark harness.** The registry route now produces a command equivalent to the driver that was removed: the served bundle path lands in `--model`, `--num-warmups` is honored, `--tokenizer` passes through with no literal `--` leaking into the child argv, and `--extra-body` comes out as `{"extra_params":{...},"seed":42}`. The new `dict()` copy of `task_extra_body` also stops `--request-seed` from leaking into a later run in the same sweep, which is easy to get wrong. No stale references to the deleted file anywhere in the tree.

**Native speed with raw/SSE.** Raw PCM streaming at speed 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 all return 200. With `seed` pinned in the request body the duration ratios are exact (1.000 / 0.667 / 0.498) and the streamed durations match the non-streaming ones to the centisecond (3.87 / 2.58 / 1.93 s), repeatable byte for byte. Out of range speed still returns a clean 400 on the streaming path and the engine stays healthy afterwards. Worth noting for anyone re-measuring: without a pinned seed the ratios wander by up to 17% purely from AR sampling variance, so it can look broken when it is not.

Test suites for the changed areas: 468 passed locally (benchmarks, speech serving, streaming, TTS adapter, indextts2).

Two things blocking the merge that are not code review items: the branch is currently `CONFLICTING` against main (`docs/models/supported_models.md`), and `buildkite/vllm-omni-amd-ci` is red on build 10374. I have not confirmed whether that AMD failure is related to this PR, so please check the failing job before assuming either way.

One note on the hardware wording in the validation comment. Reporting it as L20X rather than H200 is the cautious choice, but it likely undersells the measurement: on that machine `nvidia-smi` shows the `NVIDIA L20X` name while the CUDA runtime reports compute capability 9.0, 132 SMs and 141 GB of HBM3e. Quoting what the CUDA runtime reports, rather than the NVML product name, would describe the box more accurately without overclaiming.

The remaining inline comments are all non-blocking.
